summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, atrial fibrillation, and a history of mitral regurgitation was admitted after waking with severe shortness of breath. She was found to have acute hypoxemic respiratory failure due to volume overload and pulmonary edema. She was stabilized with CPAP and nitroglycerin, and underwent urgent hemodialysis, which improved her symptoms. Repeat imaging showed resolution of pulmonary edema. A lung opacity was deemed more likely asymmetric edema than infection, and antibiotics were discontinued. An echocardiogram revealed worsening mitral regurgitation and pulmonary hypertension, prompting a cardiology follow-up. She had a transient episode of atrial fibrillation during dialysis but remained stable. A known pancreatic cyst was noted, with plans for repeat imaging in six months. She was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments and follow-up plans for sleep study, cardiology, and dialysis management.
